description: Real ClinicalTrials.gov eligibility criteria paired with hand-written profiles. MET means the criterion, as written, describes the person — including for exclusion criteria, where that is what rules them out (docs/decisions/0004). Labels marked needs_human_review are proposals and are not scored until a person signs them off.

pairs.criterion: * Age ≥ 22
pairs.basis: The profile states 41, and 41 is at least 22.

pairs.criterion: * Age ≥ 22
pairs.basis: The profile states 12, which is below 22.

pairs.criterion: * Age ≥ 22
pairs.basis: The profile states 34, which is at least 22.

pairs.criterion: * Living in the US
pairs.basis: The profile records no country of residence.

pairs.criterion: * Fluent in English
pairs.basis: The profile records nothing about languages spoken.

pairs.criterion: * Fatigue Severity Scale score at or above eligibility threshold
pairs.basis: The profile holds no Fatigue Severity Scale score, and no way to derive one.

pairs.criterion: * Willingness to engage in self-administration of an online intervention for 24 weeks and complete follow-up assessments
pairs.basis: Willingness is not something the profile records.

pairs.criterion: * Access to the internet and e-mail with a compatible device (smartphone, computer, or tablet)
pairs.basis: The profile says nothing about this, so nobody can answer it from what we were told.

pairs.criterion: * No MS relapse / no steroid treatment in the 4 weeks prior to answering the screening questionnaire (self-reported)
pairs.basis: The profile holds no relapse or steroid history.

pairs.criterion: * No disease-modifying therapeutic (DMT) started in the 4 weeks prior to answering the screening questionnaire (self-reported)
pairs.basis: The profile holds no treatment history.

pairs.criterion: * Unwilling or unable to consent
pairs.basis: Whether the person is able and willing to consent is not recorded.

pairs.criterion: * Concurrent participation in another interventional trial
pairs.basis: The profile records no other trial participation.

pairs.criterion: 2. Participants who have not received any BRIUMVI® (ublituximab-xiiy) infusion prior to study start. Participants who have been prescribed BRIUMVI® (ublituximab-xiiy) but have not yet received their first infusion on Day 1 of 150 milligrams (mg) can be included.
pairs.basis: The profile records no prior infusions of anything.

pairs.criterion: 1. Have received any live or live-attenuated vaccines (including for varicella-zoster virus or measles) within 4 weeks prior to first BRIUMVI® (ublituximab-xiiy) administration or any non-live vaccines within 2 weeks prior to first BRIUMVI® (ublituximab-xiiy) administration.
pairs.basis: The profile records no vaccination history.

pairs.criterion: 2. Any active infection (e.g., active Hepatitis B virus \[HBV\])
pairs.basis: The profile records no infections.

pairs.criterion: 3. Concurrent participation in any interventional MS trials, or planned concurrent treatment with other Multiple Sclerosis Disease Modifying Therapy (MS DMT) during the study period.
pairs.basis: The profile records no other trial participation.

pairs.criterion:
* Meets at least 1 of the following criteria for disease activity:

  i) At least 1 MS relapse/attack in the previous year prior to screening.
pairs.basis: The profile holds no relapse or MRI history.

pairs.criterion: ii) At least 2 MS relapses/attacks in the previous 2 years prior to screening.
pairs.basis: The profile holds no relapse count.

pairs.criterion: iii) Evidence of 1 or more gadolinium-enhancing (GdE) lesions on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) within 6 months prior to baseline (including screening MRI).
pairs.basis: The profile holds no MRI findings.

pairs.criterion: \- Has an Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score of 0 to 5.5, both inclusive.
pairs.basis: The profile holds no EDSS score.

pairs.criterion: * Active or chronic disease of the immune system other than MS.
pairs.basis: The profile lists one condition and says nothing about immune disease.

pairs.criterion: * Clinically relevant cardiovascular, hepatic, neurological other major systematic disease.
pairs.basis: The profile records no cardiovascular, hepatic or neurological disease.

pairs.criterion: * Other protocol-defined Inclusion/Exclusion criteria apply.
pairs.basis: The criterion refers to requirements not published in the record, so nobody outside the study can answer it.

pairs.criterion: * Confirmed diagnosis of MS by a physician, who is a neurologist or has access to a neurologist's statement of diagnosis
pairs.basis: The profile lists no conditions at all, so whether they have a confirmed MS diagnosis is unanswerable.

pairs.criterion: * Fatigue Severity Scale score at or above eligibility threshold
pairs.basis: The profile says nothing about this, so nobody can answer it from what we were told.

pairs.criterion: 1. Confirmed Multiple Sclerosis (MS) diagnosis.
pairs.basis: The profile lists no conditions, so an MS diagnosis cannot be confirmed or ruled out.

pairs.criterion: * Informed consent by person with MS
pairs.basis: Proposed UNKNOWN: the profile records a condition, not whether consent has been given. A reviewer should confirm that consent is never inferable from a profile.

pairs.criterion: * Confirmed diagnosis of MS by a physician, who is a neurologist or has access to a neurologist's statement of diagnosis
pairs.basis: Proposed UNKNOWN: the person says they have MS, but the criterion asks for a diagnosis confirmed by a neurologist, which their own statement does not establish. A reviewer must decide whether self-reported diagnosis should ever count as MET.

pairs.criterion: * Has a diagnosis of multiple sclerosis (MS) as defined by the 2017 revision of the McDonald Criteria with a relapsing remitting course of disease.
pairs.basis: Proposed UNKNOWN: the person states relapsing-remitting MS, but the criterion requires diagnosis by the 2017 McDonald criteria, which is a clinical determination. A reviewer must decide.

pairs.criterion: 1. Confirmed Multiple Sclerosis (MS) diagnosis.
pairs.basis: Proposed UNKNOWN: same question as the McDonald-criteria pair — does a self-reported diagnosis satisfy 'confirmed'? A reviewer should answer it once, consistently, for every pair like this.

pairs.criterion: 2. Participants who have not received any BRIUMVI® (ublituximab-xiiy) infusion prior to study start. Participants who have been prescribed BRIUMVI® (ublituximab-xiiy) but have not yet received their first infusion on Day 1 of 150 milligrams (mg) can be included.
pairs.basis: The criterion describes participants who have NOT received a BRIUMVI infusion before the study. This profile lists BRIUMVI among past treatments, so the sentence does not describe them. No clinical judgement: the drug is named in the criterion and named in the profile.

pairs.criterion: 2. Participants who have not received any BRIUMVI® (ublituximab-xiiy) infusion prior to study start. Participants who have been prescribed BRIUMVI® (ublituximab-xiiy) but have not yet received their first infusion on Day 1 of 150 milligrams (mg) can be included.
pairs.basis: The profile lists ocrelizumab and interferon beta-1a and no BRIUMVI, so as far as we were told they have not had one, and the sentence describes them.

pairs.criterion: * No disease-modifying therapeutic (DMT) started in the 4 weeks prior to answering the screening questionnaire (self-reported)
pairs.basis: The profile says they are on a disease-modifying therapy but not when it was started, and the criterion is about the last four weeks. A treatment list narrows this and does not settle it.

pairs.criterion: * Has a diagnosis of multiple sclerosis (MS) as defined by the 2017 revision of the McDonald Criteria with a relapsing remitting course of disease.
pairs.basis: Proposed UNKNOWN: the profile states relapsing-remitting MS diagnosed in 2019, which is closer than a bare condition name, but the criterion requires diagnosis by the 2017 McDonald criteria and that remains a clinical determination. A reviewer should settle this the same way as the other self-reported-diagnosis pairs.

pairs.criterion: * Diagnosis of progressive forms of MS.
pairs.basis: Proposed NOT_MET: this is an EXCLUSION criterion and MET would mean the person has progressive MS. They state relapsing-remitting, which is not a progressive form, so the sentence does not describe them. A reviewer must confirm both the clinical claim and that the polarity convention in docs/decisions/0004 was applied correctly — this is the pair most likely to be scored backwards.
